newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Court hearing on bail of Begum Zia's son adjourned.
newsitem.headline: Court hearing on bail of Begum Zia's son adjourned.

text.p: Bangladesh's High Court on Sunday adjourned the hearing of bail petitions by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia's son and brother, who face corruption charges, court officials said.
The court put off the hearing until Monday but asked the police not to arrest them till it ruled on the case.

Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Bureau filed charges against Tareq Rahman and his uncle Syeed Iskander on September 16, saying they overvalued land used as partial collateral when borrowing 153 million taka ($3.8 million) from the state-owned Sonali Bank to set up a textile dyeing company.
Police said the accused put a value 1.8 million taka on land worth only 120,000 taka.
Rahman and Iskander applied on Wednesday for "anticipatory bail. Hundreds of supporters crowded the High Court as judges began hearing their petitions on Sunday.
"The bank is not the complainant but the government. Moreover it's a case of civil nature and can never be a criminal case," their lawyer Moudud Ahmed told reporters on Sunday.
Ahmed said he had argued that the case against his clients was "politically motivated" and aimed to "defame and disrepute" the former prime minister and her family.
